summary.headline: Gland Pharma Q1 FY27 revenue rose 20% YoY to INR18,003 million, adjusted EBITDA margin 28%, PAT up 47% to INR3,170 million.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 20% YoY to INR18,003 million, with CDMO and B2B each about 50% of sales and U.S. revenue up 32%. Adjusted EBITDA (after adding back ESOP) was INR5,102 million at 28% margin, up from 25%, while reported EBITDA was INR4,930 million after a INR36 million forex loss. PAT rose 47% YoY to INR3,170 million but fell versus Q4 FY26, which had a INR508 million forex gain. Management announced a 55-SKU, USD90-100 million potential CDMO supply deal, a China-sourced liposomal in-licence, and a INR2,000 crore capex programme now being executed; Saudi Arabia NUPCO tender delays hit rest-of-world sales.

financial_highlights.metric: Reported EBITDA (after forex loss INR36 million)

financial_highlights.change: +47% YoY; down vs Q4 FY26 due to forex swing
+16% YoY from INR664 million; up from INR723 million in Q4 FY26

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR8,915 million, +20% YoY, 50% of total. Growth from recent launches and existing commercial programmes; new GLP-1 contract (semaglutide and tirzepatide, U.S. and EU) signed this quarter.

segments.name: B2B
segments.commentary: Revenue INR9,088 million, +19% YoY, 50% of total, driven by existing customers, new contract wins and higher volumes.

segments.name: United States
segments.commentary: Revenue INR9,810 million, +32% YoY, largest market; 4 products launched in the quarter including MVI and Dalbavancin.

segments.name: Rest of world
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,039 million, broadly flat YoY; Saudi Arabia supply disruptions as NUPCO tender awards are delayed.

segments.name: Cenexi (Europe)
segments.commentary: Revenue EUR48 million (flat YoY) and EBITDA EUR2 million (~4% margin); heat wave disrupted Fontenay, with quality releases delayed into Q2.

guidance_outlook: Constant-currency growth for FY27 is targeted at about 15%; management said it could exceed 15% if the new bag line gets FDA approval in Aug-Sep 2026.
Over the next 4 years, management is working toward roughly 20% growth; a fuller update is planned for the next quarter or by Aug-Oct 2026.
Consolidated EBITDA target of 30% near term, with 35% over 3-4 years; CDMO and B2B split targeted at about 50:50 for the next 2 years, with CDMO possibly larger after CY29.
Cenexi FY27 guidance maintained at about EUR200 million revenue with high single-digit EBITDA margin; management expects Q2 to be better than last year.
New 55-SKU CDMO agreement: tech transfer starts September 2026, revenue from CY29, USD90-100 million potential once all products are commercialised.
Liposomal in-licence (China partner, U.S. and EU rights): commercial revenue from FY30. NDDS project: completion 2028, commercialisation 2029, revenue potential USD25-30 million.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR2,000 crore programme has started; INR550 crore planned for this year. An isolator line for oncology costs about INR165 crore and is expected to be installed in January 2027.
Ongoing India projects (vial, ophthalmic, BFS lines and liposome) are on track; Suite 10 at Pashamylaram is being added for vial, BFS and ophthalmic lines.
Fontenay (Cenexi) will replace an older ampoule line with a new high-capacity line adding about 30 million ampoules a year, production expected early 2027.
Vial and lyophilisation build at BLA and high-speed and ampoule line at Fontenay are due for completion by end of next year (2027).
New Neuland API sterile suite is under construction; current capacity is fully occupied.
demand_pricing: Management says generic pricing pressure opens a door for CDMO, as large pharma seek lower-cost sites (Europe is said to be 5-6x costlier than India).
U.S. revenue growth of 32% was helped by launches; the base business (ex-Cenexi) grew 24% in total, with about 19-20% in constant currency.
GLP-1 contribution is expected to be very limited over the next few years beyond tech-transfer fees; volume is expected from the U.S. in FY30-31.
Profit share with partners on the IP-owned business is about 9% of the quarter's profit.

qa_highlights.question: Details on the 55-SKU strategic manufacturing deal, and how fast will revenue ramp to USD90-100 million?
qa_highlights.answer: Partner is a global specialty pharma company; about 30-40% of revenue is specialty. Products are made in Indian sites; split is about 60% U.S., 30-35% Europe, 15-20% ROW. Tech transfer starts September 2026, first products in 24 months, ramp from 2029 to 2030.

qa_highlights.question: Revised capex estimate?
qa_highlights.answer: INR550 crore to be spent this year, with the INR165 crore oncology isolator line as a priority; brownfield or greenfield expansion is being planned.

qa_highlights.question: Constant-currency growth for the quarter on a consolidated basis?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 15%. It explained the FX calculation uses the rate on each dispatch date, and guidance is set on a constant-currency basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is Cenexi turning around, and what is its profitability outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 EBITDA was about 4% margin, similar to the trend; management targets double-digit EBITDA by year-end. Q2 should beat last year because some quality releases slipped from Q1 because of the heat wave.

qa_highlights.question: GLP-1 scale-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: New line on track, with exhibit batches for several customers; transfers in the next 1-2 quarters. Revenue potential over 3 years is very limited; Canada launch could be upside.

qa_highlights.question: Are there patent-protected products in the CDMO base, and is the pipeline biologics or peptides?
qa_highlights.answer: No innovative products currently; some 505(b)(2) products have patents. Pipeline discussions are on peptides, not biologics. Biologics (Dr. Reddy's partnership) generate about INR50-60 crore a year.

risks_watch: Saudi Arabia NUPCO tender awards are delayed, and rest-of-world revenue was flat YoY.
Forex swings: Q1 had a INR36 million forex loss after a INR508 million gain in Q4 FY26, which drove the sequential PAT decline.
Capacity constraints in bag line and ophthalmic products; the bag line needs FDA approval in Q3 FY27.
Cenexi profitability (about 4% EBITDA) and the EUR200 million FY27 target need to be delivered; the heat wave hit Q1.
Large complex-injectable and microsphere opportunities are mostly post-FY29, so near-term growth depends on launches and CDMO ramp-ups.
Revised 4-year CAGR (around 20%) and constant-currency FY27 growth to be confirmed next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on CDMO and capacity, with clear targets for FY27 and beyond. Management was more cautious on rest-of-world (Saudi tender delays), on GLP-1 revenue timing, and in declining to give numbers on several questions (e.g. Cenexi, product sizes, launch pipeline).
key_quotes: We have started FY27 with a strong momentum, delivering healthy year-on-year growth in revenues, EBITDA and profit after tax.
To be fair, without Cenexi, this wouldn't have happened in a way.
So today, we are at 28% consol EBITDA percent. So near term, we're working towards 30% and we'll see midterm to long term.
